title: Week 5: From Design to Implementation
text: Week four ended with the analytical and back-end architecture for phase four prepared. During week five, I implemented and integrated that architecture as an end-to-end decision intelligence system. The objective was to move Causal Couture beyond a static scorecard. The platform would now support current condition analysis, changing pattern detection, hypothetical simulation, and structured decision support recommendations. title: End-to-End Workflow Integration Testing
text: Framework's response to user-defined assumptions without claiming those conditions will occur or that one variable causally produces another. I implemented trend intelligence to add temporal context. The system divides available chronological data into previous and recent periods, then compares demand, inventory, engagement, and conversion. Trends are summarized with percentage change and readable directions such as increasing, declining, or stable. A trend snapshot makes these recent changes visible alongside the current analytical state. I also implemented a rule-based business alert engine. It evaluates combinations of analytical and trend signals to surface conditions that may require business attention. Supported conditions include high demand with falling inventory, high stock risk, high engagement with weak conversion, conversion decline, demand acceleration, and engagement momentum. When none of the supported major conditions is detected, the system can explicitly communicate that no major alerts are currently present. The executive dashboard aggregation layer combines the major analytical outputs into one response. KPI, trends, recommendation, alerts, data set summary,

And data source status. Data set summary includes row count, column count, unique SKU count, and date range. Source status identifies whether sales, inventory, social, and web information is available in the unified data set. I integrated these capabilities into the phase API back end through dedicated phase four end points for dashboard intelligence and scenario analysis. I also implemented four scenario presets. Demand surge, inventory pressure, engagement without conversion and softening demand. These presets let users explore common fashion retail situations without configuring every variable manually. Users can still modify demand, inventory, engagement and conversion through the individual scenario controls. I then integrated the phase four back end into a redesigned front end organized around five sections. Overview, data, intelligence, scenario lab and insights. Overview presents primary KPIs and analytical state. Data supports source processing and unified data set generation. Intelligence presents recommendations and context. Scenario lab provides interactive controls. Insights surfaces alerts and supporting analysis. The redesigned experience includes

Sticky navigation, active section highlighting, smooth scrolling, page progress, responsive layouts, loading and notification states, empty states, collapsible technical output, scenario feedback, interaction feedback, keyboard focus, back to top navigation and clearer hierarchy. I tested the complete workflow. Upload data, validate and process, build the unified data set, load intelligence, analyze trends, review alerts, configure a scenario, run the simulation and compare results. Both manual scenario controls and preset scenarios were tested. I also verified front end to back end communication and confirmed that the returned analytical results were displayed through the redesigned interface. By the end of week five, phase four was complete as an end-to-end system combining modular analytics, scenario simulation, trend analysis, alerts, structured recommendations, dashboard aggregation, an interactive scenario lab, and a redesigned front end. This creates the foundation for the next development direction, causal intelligence. Future work will move beyond observed signals and hypothetical simulations toward formally estimated causal effects. I'm Ushasvi Rachel for Humanitarian's AI.
